about: The names the network's lookups may be answered for once the DNS policy blocks the rest (S68 audit finding 14; dns-policy.bicep). Each entry is a name or a zone ending in a dot, and covers every name under it. Read from three days of staging's lookups (S78, 30 Sep to 3 Oct 2026), each one Microsoft's or GitHub's; names Microsoft picks and changes (storage accounts, the cluster's API host) are allowed by their zone. Not listed on purpose: reverse lookups (Azure sends them to public servers, which answer that no such name exists), and the login service's internal address (answered inside the environment: it never appears in the logs). This narrows which names are answered; whether a blocked name's labels still reach its own server (Azure follows CNAME chains, so it may resolve a name before judging it) is proven before relying on it (Carry-Forward). The policy's dns-allow rule refuses any Allow not listed here.
